atomic.decision: Public package, version, entry and documented module imports share one identity.
Ordinary Task normalization preserves identity, actions, documentation and metadata.
A dependency-only group preserves graph identity without inventing a body action.
dict_to_task accepts an ordinary definition and rejects unsupported or incomplete mappings.
Python actions preserve success, result, value, failure and error categories.
Command actions preserve list argument boundaries and nonzero failure status.
run_once and config_changed expose committed freshness semantics.
Directory creation and target cleaning are idempotent and scope-preserving.
Prepared task definitions remain invisible until committed.
Definition revisions are idempotent, monotonic and conflict-rejecting.
Selection plans own canonical dependency closure and one invocation generation.
Selection handoff fences the old owner without changing the canonical closure.
Task attempts separate prepared, terminal and acknowledged result state.
Target artifact publication is exact-byte, atomic and verifiable.
Setup, body and reverse teardown are durable distinct obligations.
Reporter events separate prepare, publish, claim and acknowledgement.

composition.decision: Module loading, generated identities and selected dependency closure agree.
One selected branch runs its dependency once while an unrelated branch stays excluded.
Action result values and freshness helpers agree across a corrected rerun.
Target ownership, file dependency selection and scoped cleaning close without sibling mutation.
A committed definition revision is the only revision selectable by a fresh invocation.
Failed definition replacement preserves the last runnable revision and its result.
Reopened definition and target index retain one revision identity after relocation.
Overlapping name, group and target requests deduplicate one canonical closure.
A stale selection owner cannot begin or acknowledge a task attempt.
Invocation-local handoff changes reporter ownership without importing a previous selection.
Only tasks admitted by the current selection may create result attempts.
Failure after a tentative value publishes neither value nor freshness and still unwinds lifecycle.
Completed-unacknowledged task recovery verifies targets and acknowledges exactly once.
A failed task remains a terminal failure event and cannot be published as success.
Target manifests bind the task definition revision that produced their bytes.
An interrupted artifact prepare exposes no current target and recovers atomically.
Changed input invalidates one target generation while an unchanged sibling remains current.
Artifact corruption fails closed before a target-success event becomes visible.
Setup obligations are admitted only for stale selected tasks.
Nested setup unwinds executed frames in reverse after body failure.
Target publication waits for all lifecycle obligations and rollback leaves prior bytes.
Lifecycle events preserve setup/body/teardown order across reopen and retry.
Committed task results create one ordered reporter batch and retry delivery exactly once.
A stale publisher cannot claim or acknowledge events after selection handoff.
Discovery, dependency execution, result publication and a fresh currentness view close through public APIs.
Failure, corrected selection, target effect and clean view agree through Python and module entry surfaces.
A complete selected task generation closes definition, attempt, target, lifecycle and reporter receipts.
Action failure preserves the prior acknowledged generation and corrected retry publishes once.
Ownership transfer fences stale work and a fresh process resumes the same receipt closure.
Overlapping selection converges while failed independent work cannot pollute the winning branch.
Crash between complete and acknowledgement recovers exactly once without duplicate action or event.
Corrupt or cyclic closure fails closed and leaves the last acknowledged task generation visible.
